contentBlocks.text: You've learned digestion and circulation. Today: the respiratory system, and its close partnership with circulation!

The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide, mainly through the lungs. But the lungs alone can't get oxygen to the rest of the body — that's where yesterday's circulatory system comes in: blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and carries it everywhere else. Explain how the respiratory and circulatory systems depend on each other to get oxygen to your whole body.
You just learned how two body systems depend on each other! Tomorrow we'll see how three systems together power your whole body.

objectives: Name the respiratory system's main function: bringing in oxygen, removing carbon dioxide
Explain the interdependence between the respiratory and circulatory systems
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's digestive and circulatory-system work.
2. Introduce the respiratory system and its lungs.
3. Discuss the respiratory-circulatory interdependence.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's three-systems synthesis lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a simple 'lungs load oxygen onto blood, blood delivers it' analogy, like a delivery truck picking up and dropping off packages
Ready for more: ask the child what might happen to the rest of the body if the respiratory system stopped working, even if circulation still worked fine
This lesson explicitly builds the 'systems interacting together' idea toward tomorrow's full-synthesis lesson
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an explanation activity — check that the child correctly explains the lungs bring in oxygen, but need the circulatory system to actually carry that oxygen to the rest of the body's cells.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 6-8 Life Science standard MS-LS1-3, continuing this week's body-systems thread with a third interacting system.

generationData.instructions: Explain how the respiratory and circulatory systems depend on each other.
